A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same O-FCL research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original classification experiments on natural images, biomedical images, and text, together with ablations, runtime measurements, and generated-image examples.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds TinyImageNet results, a CIFAR100 task-count study, and image-resolution timing measurements.

M1.justification: The BI estimator, class-balanced memory selection, random replay, communication schedule, and parameter aggregation procedures remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 is retained verbatim in substance, moving from Appendix A.9 to A.11.

E1.justification: v4 adds TinyImageNet, with 200 classes and 64×64 images, to the existing natural-image classification coverage (Section 4.1 and Appendix A.4). All previous datasets remain; biomedical and textual task coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged. The added studies reuse existing baselines. FedCIL remains in the original comparisons and is marked unevaluated on the newly added TinyImageNet benchmark because of its stated image-size restriction.

E3.justification: Added protocols use ten TinyImageNet tasks, evaluate CIFAR100 with 5, 10, 20, and 25 tasks, and measure mini-batch processing time at resolutions from 32×32 to 224×224. Previously documented architectures, optimizers, batch size, communication settings, and accuracy/forgetting metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds focused analyses of forgetting under longer task sequences (Appendix A.7, Table 12) and processing latency as image resolution increases (A.9, Table 15). Existing hyperparameter ablations, communication analysis, total-runtime comparisons, and generated-image examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments use three random seeds and report benchmark results with ± values. TinyImageNet follows this practice; the new task-count table uses point estimates like the existing ablations. No new uncertainty-estimation procedure or significance testing is documented.

E6.justification: Existing result entries remain unchanged. New Table 7 reports TinyImageNet BI accuracy/forgetting of 11.04/6.07 versus ER's 11.26/6.31. Table 12 adds longer-sequence results, including 25-task BI accuracy/forgetting of 13.71/33.65, and Table 15 adds resolution-dependent timings. Table 12 also lists five-task BI forgetting as 8.96, whereas retained Tables 2 and 5 give 6.96; no setting distinction explains this discrepancy.

T1.justification: The online-FCL formulation, BI expression, alternative uncertainty-score definitions, and accuracy/forgetting equations are unchanged. No theorem, proof, formal assumption, or mathematical derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about online FCL, BI-based memory management, reduced forgetting, multimodal applicability, and communication efficiency. The additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v4 explains increasing forgetting through the difficulty of retaining early tasks over longer sequences and adds an argument that online scalability is governed by per-batch processing and image size (Appendices A.7 and A.9). Existing limitations concerning TTA cost and BI-estimator underestimation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: A new reproducibility statement supplies a code repository link and states that preprocessing scripts and experiment instructions are available there. Existing hardware and training details are reiterated, while Table 15 adds per-batch runtime information. These are documentation additions, without evidence of an implementation revision.

R1.justification: v4 adds Le and Yang's TinyImageNet reference in connection with the new benchmark. The related-work discussion and positioning against continual-learning and federated-learning approaches remain substantively unchanged; other citation changes are stylistic.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order are retained. v4 adds a reproducibility statement and short appendix passages, including an explanation of the unchanged Figure 3, and updates cross-references and publication/header text. There is no extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v4 adds Tables 7, 12, and 15 and a TinyImageNet row in Table 6. Existing figures and table structures are retained, with appendix material repositioned and renumbered. The conference template changes title, author, heading, and caption formatting without substantially redesigning the displays.

improvement.justification: Compared with v3, v4 modestly strengthens validation through TinyImageNet and longer task sequences, documents resolution-dependent processing costs, and provides explicit code-access information. These improve empirical support and reproducibility guidance while preserving the original method and results. The gains are limited by incomplete settings for the added experiments, including TinyImageNet's unspecified memory size, and the unexplained five-task forgetting discrepancy between new Table 12 and retained Tables 2 and 5.
